fi-ecsenius-bicolor.title: Bicolor Blenny
fi-ecsenius-bicolor.summary: A personable perching blenny, blue-brown in front and orange behind. Grazes algae on the rocks.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 11 cm (4.3 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Usually fine, but an underfed fish may nip clam mantles or fleshy LPS
Herbivore. Feed algae-based frozen and dried foods; it also grazes algae in the tank
Indo-Pacific: Maldives to the Phoenix Islands, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef; throughout Micronesia
notes: Needs rocks to perch on and holes to hide in; in the wild it lives in empty worm tubes.
May pick on other blennies, small gobies and dartfish.

fi-salarias-fasciatus.title: Lawnmower Blenny
fi-salarias-fasciatus.summary: A peaceful, comical algae grazer with big eyes and a mottled tan body. Also sold as the Sailfin or Algae Blenny.
rows: About 5 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep singly unless a mated pair in a larger tank
Listed reef compatible, but known to nip small-polyp stony corals and clam mantles
Herbivore. Grazes microalgae; supplement with vegetable matter, spirulina and herbivore foods
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia
notes: Does best in an established tank with lots of natural algae and rockwork.
Lives on shallow reef flats in the wild, even brackish edges.

fi-ophioblennius-atlanticus.title: Redlip Blenny
fi-ophioblennius-atlanticus.summary: A Caribbean blenny with a blunt "horse face", red lips and dark body. Spends its time hopping between rocks grazing.
rows: About 5 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 19 cm (7.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep singly unless a mated pair in a larger tank
Listed reef compatible, but may nip small-polyp stony corals and clam mantles
Herbivore. Needs plenty of natural microalgae; supplement with algae foods
Atlantic Ocean: oceanic islands and along the coast of west Africa from Senegal to Angola
notes: Aggressive mainly toward fish shaped like itself.
warn: Has long, sharp canine teeth and can bite hard (FishBase rates it traumatogenic).

fi-salarias-ramosus.title: Starry Blenny
fi-salarias-ramosus.summary: A mottled brown combtooth blenny covered in small pearly spots, from the Philippines to north-western Australia. It grazes algae from rock all day.
rows: About 5.5 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Herbivore: needs grazing on live rock plus nori/algae sheets, spirulina and herbivore flakes, pellets or wafers
Western Central Pacific: Philippines to northwestern Australia
notes: Clashes with other blennies, gobies and algae grazers that share its food and shape; give plenty of rock to graze.

fi-meiacanthus-atrodorsalis.title: Forktail Blenny
fi-meiacanthus-atrodorsalis.summary: A sleek fang blenny that fades from pale blue at the head to bright yellow at its forked tail, with a dark line through the eye. Its venomous bite means predators leave it alone.
rows: About 5 in (LiveAquaria / Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 11 cm (4.3 in) TL (FishBase)
One per tank unless you have a breeding pair
Omnivore: chopped crustacean flesh, mysis and enriched brine shrimp plus some herbivore foods; it also picks at algae on live rock
Western Pacific: Bali and the Philippines east to Samoa, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to Rowley Shoals, the southern Great Barrier Reef
warn: Venomous bite: it can nip fingers that it sees as a threat, so take care with children around the tank.

fi-meiacanthus-grammistes.title: Striped Fang Blenny (Grammistes Blenny)
fi-meiacanthus-grammistes.summary: A fang blenny striped lengthwise in black, yellow and white, from the Western Pacific. Its small venomous fangs are for defense, and other blennies copy its look for protection.
rows: About 5 in (LiveAquaria adult size); wild record 11 cm (4.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Usually one per tank; it may squabble with similar-shaped fish
Omnivore: chopped crustaceans, enriched brine shrimp and frozen herbivore foods
Western Pacific: Indochina to Papua New Guinea, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to northwestern Australia and the Great Barrier Reef
notes: Give live rock to hunt over and hide in; corals and inverts are safe.
warn: Has a venomous defensive bite; avoid hand contact.
